script001:
# Script 001: AI for Small Business: Where to Actually Start (UK)

*Output of prompt #5. This is the template for every future script.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Target length** | ~10 minutes (~1,400 spoken words) |
| **Pillar** | 1. AI That Actually Helps |
| **Search target** | "AI for small business", "how to use AI in my business UK" |
| **Title** | AI for Small Business: Where to Actually Start (UK) |
| **Thumbnail** | You pointing at step 1 of a staircase. Text: **START HERE** |
| **CTA** | Free AI Readiness Checklist → wirral.ai |
| **Next video (end screen)** | #4 Staff Are Pasting Data Into ChatGPT |
| **Source material** | wirral.ai/insights/ai-for-small-business |

Key: **[B-ROLL]** cutaway footage · **[TEXT]** on-screen text · **[SFX]** sound effect ·
**[SCREEN]** screen recording · **[CUT]** jump cut / angle change

---

## 0:00 Hook (0–15 s)

> Most small businesses start with AI the wrong way. They buy a tool, a couple of
> people try it, and three months later nobody's using it.
>
> In the next ten minutes I'll show you the four-step way we start with every
> client, and the one question to ask before you spend a single penny.

**[TEXT]** "4 steps · 1 question · £0 to start"
**[B-ROLL]** fast montage: ChatGPT, Copilot, a cluttered desktop of unused apps
**[SFX]** soft whoosh into title card (1 s max, no long intro)

## 0:15 Quick proof (15–40 s)

> I'm [Name] from wirral.ai. We're an AI consultancy in the North West, and we've
> helped more than forty organisations, from clinics and trades firms to hotels and
> membership bodies, work out where AI actually fits.
>
> And honestly? About a third of the time the answer is "not yet" or "not there".
> So this isn't a "use AI for everything" video. It's the opposite.

**[B-ROLL]** real (permissioned) client work / wirral.ai portfolio scroll
**[TEXT]** "40+ organisations supported"

## 0:40 Setup / story (40 s–1:30)

> Here's what usually happens. The owner reads that AI will save them hours. They
> sign up to three tools. Someone uses ChatGPT to write a few social posts. Then
> it all fizzles out, because nobody decided what problem they were actually
> solving.
>
> So step one isn't a tool. It's a problem.

**[CUT]** to close-up
**[TEXT]** "Problem first. Tool second."

---

## 1:30 Step 1: Pick ONE annoying, repetitive job (1:30–3:15)

> Grab a pen. Write down the three jobs in your business that are: one, done every
> week; two, mostly the same each time; and three, nobody enjoys.
>
> Things like answering the same customer questions, writing quotes, chasing
> invoices, typing up meeting notes, writing job adverts.

**[SCREEN]** simple 3-column table: Job / Hours per week / Same every time?

> Now pick the one with the most hours. That's your first AI project. Not five.
> One.
>
> Here's a real example. A practice we worked with was spending around six hours a
> week replying to the same booking questions by email. That became the first
> project. Nothing fancy.

**[TEXT]** "Most hours + most repetitive = start here"
**[SFX]** pen tick

### Pattern interrupt (~2:45)
> Quick test: if you can't explain the job to a new starter in two minutes, it's
> not ready for AI either. Keep that in mind.

**[CUT]** to wide shot, hold up two fingers

## 3:15 Step 2: Use a safe tool you already have (3:15–5:00)

> Before you buy anything, check what you're already paying for. If you're on
> Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace, you may already have AI built in: Copilot or
> Gemini.
>
> And here's the important bit for UK businesses: use a **business** account, not a
> personal free one. Business plans generally don't use your data to train their
> models, and they give you admin controls. With a free personal account, you have
> much less control over where customer data goes.

**[SCREEN]** show where to find Copilot in Outlook / Gemini in Gmail
**[TEXT]** "Business account ≠ personal account"
**[B-ROLL]** padlock icon over a document

> Check the current terms for whichever tool you use. They change, and I'll put
> links in the description.

## 5:00 Mid-video teaser

> Step four is the one almost everyone skips, and it's the reason most AI projects
> quietly die. Stick around for that.

**[TEXT]** "Step 4 = the one everyone skips"
**[SFX]** short rising tone

## 5:10 Step 3: Write three simple rules (5:10–6:45)

> Before anyone starts, write three rules. One page, max.
>
> One: what data must **never** go into AI: customer health records, card details,
> anything you'd be embarrassed to see leaked.
> Two: a human checks everything before it goes to a customer.
> Three: which tools are approved, and nothing else.

**[SCREEN]** a one-page policy document with the three rules highlighted
**[TEXT]** "Never · Always check · Approved tools only"

> That's it. That's your first AI policy. We've got a free template, and I'll show
> you where to get it at the end.

### Pattern interrupt (~6:15)
**[B-ROLL]** quick "bad example": someone pasting a spreadsheet of customer names
into a chatbot → red X **[SFX]** buzzer (light, not cheesy)

## 6:45 Step 4: Measure it for 30 days (6:45–8:45)

> Here's the step everyone skips. Measure it.
>
> Before you start, write down how long the job takes now. Six hours a week? Write
> it down. Then run the AI version for thirty days and write down how long it takes
> now, and whether the quality held up.

**[SCREEN]** simple before/after table: "Before: 6 hrs/wk → After: ? hrs/wk"

> If it saved time and quality held, roll it out and pick the next job. If it didn't,
> stop. That's not failure, that's the system working. You've lost a month and
> nothing else.
>
> The businesses that get real value from AI aren't the ones with the fanciest tools.
> They're the ones that do this boring loop: pick a job, try it safely, measure, repeat.

**[TEXT]** "Pick → Try → Measure → Repeat"
**[B-ROLL]** loop animation

## 8:45 The one question before you spend a penny (8:45–9:30)

> And the question I promised at the start, before you pay for any AI tool or any
> consultant, including us: **"What will we stop doing, and how will we know?"**
>
> If nobody can answer that, don't spend the money yet.

**[CUT]** close-up, pause one beat
**[TEXT]** "What will we stop doing, and how will we know?"

## 9:30 Ending + CTA (9:30–10:00)

> If you want to check whether your business is actually ready for this, we've put
> together a free AI Readiness Checklist. Eight questions, takes five minutes. It's
> linked in the description and the pinned comment.
>
> And one of the biggest risks I mentioned, staff pasting customer data into
> ChatGPT, is probably already happening in your business. This video shows you
> what to do about it.

**[END SCREEN]** → Video #4 (Staff + ChatGPT) + subscribe button
**[TEXT]** "Free checklist → wirral.ai"

*(No "thanks for watching", no outro music. End on the recommendation.)*

---

## Drop-off risks and how the script fixes them

| Moment | Why viewers might leave | Fix built into the script |
|---|---|---|
| 0–5 s | Looks like another generic AI video | Opens with a contrarian claim ("most start wrong"), no logo intro |
| 0:15–0:40 | "Who is this guy?" credentials ramble | Kept to 25 s; credibility through honesty ("a third of the time, not yet") |
| ~2:00 | Step 1 feels like homework | Concrete example (6 hrs/week of booking emails) + the "new starter" test |
| ~3:30 | Talking-head fatigue | Switches to screen recording of real Copilot/Gemini |
| ~5:00 | Midpoint slump | Explicit teaser for step 4 |
| ~6:15 | Rules feel dry | Visual "bad example" + light SFX |
| ~8:30 | Viewer thinks "got it" and leaves | Promised "one question" is still unpaid; payoff held until 8:45 |
| End | Outro = exit | No outro; go straight to the next video recommendation |

---

## Shorts to cut from this video

1. **"Business account ≠ personal account"** (3:15–4:10) → hook: "Using free ChatGPT for work? Watch this."
2. **"The one question before buying AI"** (8:45–9:30) → hook: "Ask this before paying for any AI tool."
3. **"3-rule AI policy"** (5:10–6:15) → hook: "Your whole AI policy, in 3 rules."
